from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        line = Line(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color=WHITE).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(line, 'C3')
        dots = VGroup(Dot(color=WHITE), Dot(color=WHITE)).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1.5)
        self.place_at_grid(dots, 'C3')
        self.play(Transform(dot, dots))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(colors[2])
        disk = Circle(radius=0.8, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(disk, 'C3')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(colors[3])
        sphere = Sphere(radius=0.8, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(sphere, 'C3')
        self.play(Transform(disk, sphere))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(colors[4])
        formula = MathTex(r"x_1^2 + x_2^2 + \dots + x_n^2 = r^2", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'E3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Corner Problem: Cubes vs. Spheres", [
            "Consider a sphere inside a hypercube.",
            "Sphere volume vanishes relative to the cube.",
            "Corners stretch far from the center."
        ])

        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Render inscribed N-sphere
        sphere = Sphere(radius=1.25, fill_opacity=0.5, color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_in_area(sphere, 'B3', 'E6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight corner volume excess
        corners = VGroup(*[Sphere(radius=0.2, color=YELLOW).move_to(p) for p in [
            cube.get_corner(DR), cube.get_corner(DL), cube.get_corner(UR), cube.get_corner(UL)
        ]])
        self.play(FadeIn(corners))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Practical Application: High-Dimensional Data", [

            "Curse of dimensionality affects distance metrics.",
            "Distance resembles navigation on a hypersphere."

        self.play(Create(hypersphere), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN_C))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Reflection", [
            "High-dimensional geometry isn't just theory.",
            "It transforms complex data into structure.",
            "Geometry is a foundational computational tool."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        sphere = Sphere(radius=1.0, color=BLUE).set_opacity(0.5)
        # Using a VGroup of small dots to simulate a data cloud
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(point=np.random.normal(0, 0.4, 3), color=YELLOW) for _ in range(50)])
        data_cloud = self.place_in_area(dots, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Transform(sphere, data_cloud))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(Indicate(self.lecture[2]))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Geometry of High-Dimensional Spheres: Beyond 3D Intuition
outline.target_audience: University students (STEM majors) or curious lifelong learners

sections.title: Prerequisite Intuition: Expanding Dimensions
sections.content: Establish the recursive definition of a sphere. A 1D sphere is 2 points on a line, a 2D sphere (disk) is area in a plane, and a 3D sphere is volume in space. Introduce the generalized formula: x₁² + x₂² + ... + xₙ² = r².
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Flatland' character trying to grasp a 3D ball moving through their 2D world.

sections.title: The Counter-Intuitive Volume Collapse
sections.content: Explain how the volume of a hypersphere behaves as dimensions (n) increase. While the surface area grows, the volume eventually concentrates near the 'equator' or the 'shell' of the sphere, counter to 3D intuition.
sections.example: An 'Orange' analogy: In high dimensions, almost all the volume of an orange is located in the peel, leaving the center virtually empty.

sections.title: The Corner Problem: Cubes vs. Spheres
sections.content: Contrast a sphere inscribed in a hypercube. As dimensions increase, the sphere's volume relative to the cube approaches zero. The corners of the hypercube stretch further away from the center.
sections.example: A 'Robot Scout' navigating a high-dimensional warehouse; it finds that moving into the 'corners' takes vastly more energy than moving toward the sphere-like center.

sections.title: Practical Application: High-Dimensional Data
sections.content: Connect the math to Machine Learning. Explain that data points in high-dimensional feature spaces often behave as if they are on the surface of a hypersphere (the 'Curse of Dimensionality').
sections.example: A recommendation engine sorting millions of users; the distance metrics function like navigation on the surface of a hypersphere to find 'similar' neighbors.

sections.title: Summary & Reflection
sections.content: Recap the transition from geometric shapes to abstract data structures. Emphasize that high-dimensional geometry is not 'unreal,' but a foundational tool for understanding complex systems.
sections.example: A 5-second animated clip showing a 3D sphere morphing into a complex data cloud, reinforcing the bridge between geometry and information science.
